result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly put the near-invisible body text first (about 1.7:1 when recomputed) and give a coherent warm replacement palette. B is a little more proportionate because it keeps the brand's olive identity and checks contrast for the secondary button too, while A swaps in a teal and coral palette. A's ratios are slightly more accurate (B's link and error-on-background figures run a bit high), and A says more plainly that the accents don't stand apart from the page. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly name low text-on-background contrast as the main problem and replace the colors with a warm cream, charcoal and dark-primary scheme. B's hand-calculated ratios are more accurate: text is about 1.7:1, links 2.0:1 and the error color 2.5:1, while A overstates these a little at 1.8, 2.2 and 2.8. B also says more directly that the buttons don't stand out and nothing tells you what to tap. A is more proportionate because it keeps the original olive identity, whereas B moves the brand to teal and coral.
